source.title: Multifaceted Feature Visualization: Uncovering the Different Types of Features Learned By Each Neuron in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Anh Nguyen; Jason Yosinski; Jeff Clune

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary information are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies multifaceted neuron responses using visualization, but does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity pressure, or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative results about neurons responding to varied image types and discusses possible interpretations, including amalgams and distributed representations. These are related to polysemanticity but do not test why such responses arise or whether features are superposed. The authors also compare visualization methods and regularizers; those comparisons do not test the claim.
record.test_reason: Qualitative visualization of multifaceted neurons in an ImageNet CNN (CaffeNet). It observes neurons responding to diverse concepts, especially in fc6/fc7, but never tests why. It runs no toy sparse-feature models, no capacity analysis and no dictionary learning, and studies no LLM. The authors offer impure facets, amalgams and distributed codes as untested, non-exclusive hypotheses. Their Deconv/LRP follow-up was explicitly inconclusive. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that MFV reveals that neurons at all levels are multifaceted, more so at higher layers, and that it improves activation-maximization image quality. For fc6/fc7 units they say these seem to be amalgams of different concepts. They give alternative, non-exclusive explanations: impure facets, distributed representations, or a shared low-level cue such as goggle-like outlines. They state that the precise function of these units remains unclear, and that Deconv/LRP did not resolve it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses t-SNE, k-means clustering, and activation-maximization visualizations of ImageNet neurons; it does not use the sparse-feature toy-network method in the cited original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Facet diversity depended on layer in the reported qualitative comparison; the number of facets was manually set to k=10.

fits_no_version.finding: In CaffeNet, facet diversity of neurons increases from conv3 upward. Hidden fully connected units (fc6/fc7) respond to very different concepts, e.g. one unit fires for turtles, scuba divers, sharks, bells, faces and trucks. Their activation-maximization reconstructions often converge to the same hybrid image regardless of initialization. fc8 class units are mostly purer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ImageNet-trained CNNs, hidden fully connected neurons are often polysemantic-looking (respond to semantically unrelated inputs), more so than output class neurons. The cause (amalgam, distributed code, or a shared low-level cue) is unresolved.

record.problems: The relevant neuron results are qualitative and use hand-picked examples. The authors state that the true number of facets is not automatically identified and that the precise functions of hidden fully connected units remain unclear.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweeps, near-orthogonal directions or geometry.
All: no analysis of capacity competition or feature importance.
All: polysemantic-looking units are reported, but no alternative mechanism is tested or shown.
All: no LLMs and no dictionary/SAE recovery.
All: no analysis of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: This is a pre-superposition-era vision paper, likely cited as early evidence of polysemantic neurons. Its results are qualitative, rest on hand-picked examples and use no controls. The authors' passing mention of 'distributed representations' is speculation, not a test of superposition. The reader's T6/discusses classification is retained.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse features exceeding dimensionality, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, and sharing by other features.
Whether polysemanticity arises from mechanisms other than capacity pressure, and whether it is evidence of superposition.
LLM feature distribution across neurons and recovery of sparse features by a dictionary or SAE.
Whether dictionary features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: CaffeNet
rows.size_stated: fc6 and fc7 have 4096 outputs; fc8 has 1000 outputs
rows.stage_stated: Trained on the 1.3-million-image ILSVRC 2012 ImageNet dataset
rows.operation_detail: Multifaceted feature visualization of example neurons using clustered highly activating images and activation maximization
rows.measure: Qualitative diversity of visualized neuron facets across layers
rows.value: Neurons in layers 1 and 2 did not have noticeably different facets; starting from layer 3, facet differences increased, with higher-layer neurons described as more complex and diverse.
rows.note: A qualitative result about multifaceted responses, not feature superposition or capacity.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. This is a qualitative, hand-picked observation that facet diversity rises with layer in a CNN. It does not measure superposition, capacity or LLM feature spread.

rows.subject: CaffeNet
rows.stage_stated: Trained on the 1.3-million-image ILSVRC 2012 ImageNet dataset
rows.operation_detail: Visualized facets of fc6 and fc7 units using activation maximization initialized from mean images of clusters of highly activating validation images
rows.measure: Types of images activating hidden fully connected units and similarity of facet reconstructions across initializations
rows.value: The paper reports that many fc6 and fc7 units respond to very different image concepts and that their facet reconstructions often converge to similar images. One fc6 unit responds to turtles, scuba divers, sharks, bells, human faces, and trucks; its visualizations consistently resemble a turtle with goggles even when initialized from different concepts.
rows.uncertainty: The authors say the precise feature detected is unclear.
rows.locator: Section 3.2; Supplementary Section S3; Figures 5 and S5
rows.note: The paper offers possible interpretations such as amalgamated concepts or distributed representations, but does not establish a cause.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. Mixed-concept fc6/fc7 units are polysemantic-looking, but the cause is unestablished and the system is a vision CNN, not an LLM (V4), so it bears on no version as stated. The value is accurately paraphrased from Sec. S3 and Fig. S5c.
